topic: MLOps, Experiment Tracking, and Model Versioning
learningObjectives: Explain why experiment tracking is important in machine learning projects.
Track model versions, parameters, metrics, and artifacts.
Design a basic workflow for reproducible machine learning experiments.

activities.title: MLOps Lifecycle
activities.instruction: Explore the stages of a repeatable machine learning lifecycle.

content.concept: MLOps organizes model development, deployment, monitoring, and maintenance into a repeatable lifecycle.

descriptions: Prepare reliable data for model development.
Train models using selected data and configurations.
Make an approved model available to applications.
Track model behavior and system performance in production.
Update, retrain, or replace models when required.

activities.title: Experiment Anatomy
activities.instruction: Identify the information that should be recorded for a machine learning experiment.

content.concept: Experiment records can contain parameters, metrics, datasets, code versions, environment details, and model artifacts.

descriptions: Uniquely identifies a particular experiment run.
Identifies which dataset or data snapshot was used.
Records values such as learning rate or tree depth.
Stores results such as accuracy, F1, MAE, or RMSE.
Identifies the source-code version used for the run.
Stores the trained model produced by the experiment.

activities.title: Version Control Explorer
activities.instruction: Match each model version to the change that produced it.

content.concept: Model versioning allows teams to identify, compare, reproduce, and roll back model releases.
